description: Updates come on the 1st and the 15th, grouped, and are merged once main's required checks pass, unless they raise a major version. release-please collects the fix(deps) ones in the release pull request, which is merged by hand.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes come at once, outside the schedule.

packageRules.description: The library, pinned exactly in the manifest Home Assistant installs from and in the tests, and moved in both together. A new version reaches users, so it is a fix release-please releases. A major version is a migration done by hand (see #35): a range would let Home Assistant install a major the integration isn't written for.
The test dependencies, which no release contains.

pytest-homeassistant-custom-component pins the Home Assistant version the tests run against, betas included, which Renovate can't tell from a stable release. Its PR waits for review: check that it pins a stable release, and move the packages Home Assistant pins (below) to that release's versions in the same PR.

Packages Home Assistant pins exactly: the tests use the versions of the Home Assistant release that pytest-homeassistant-custom-component pins, moved by hand with it, not the newest on PyPI. None is a test dependency yet; the modbus stack becomes one with 2.0.0 (#35).
The Home Assistant container for manual testing, which no release contains.
Home Assistant's validation actions have no releases worth following; their branch head's digest is enough.
A major version waits for review.
